note: Parenti et al. demonstrate that MAU2 truncating variants lead to haploinsufficiency and NIPBL reduction with distinct episignatures compared to in-frame variants, providing strong biological plausibility for genotype-phenotype divergence in classic facial dysmorphism.

evidence.text: Parenti et al. described 18 individuals carrying 15 heterozygous MAU2 variants and showed that in-frame variants primarily impair NIPBL-MAU2 interaction whereas truncating variants cause haploinsufficiency and secondary NIPBL reduction, accompanied by two variant-dependent episignatures and a spectrum ranging from classic CdLS to milder presentations.

source.title: Pathogenic variants in the cohesin loader subunit MAU2 lead to a new Cornelia de Lange Syndrome subtype
source.quote: MAU2 in-frame variants predominantly impair NIPBL–MAU2 interaction, whereas truncating variants cause MAU2 haploinsufficiency and lead to NIPBL reduction. Most patients exhibit a DNA methylation profile compatible with the CdLS episignature. We also identified two MAU2-specific episignatures that reflect variant-dependent molecular consequences. Affected individuals display a wide range of phenotypes, from classic CdLS to milder presentations, with short stature and microcephaly as consistent features.
